core_obligations: Two-out-of-three reduction: note that the result holds when M has finite length, and that for a short exact sequence of modules satisfying (1) and (2) the statement for two of the three implies it for the third, by additivity of length and of multiplicities; use this to replace M by the sum of its images M_i in the localisations at the height one primes, reducing to the case where the support is exactly {m, q} (proof lines 329-346).

One-dimensional reduction: take the q-adic filtration of M, which terminates because a power of q kills M, and apply additivity again to reduce to the case where q M = 0, so that M is a module over the one-dimensional Noetherian local domain R/q with fraction field K; dividing by the torsion submodule (which has finite length) one may assume M is a lattice inside V = M tensor_R K (proof lines 347-360).

Lattice computation: then x acts injectively on M, length_R(M/xM) is the distance d(M, xM), and since det(x : V -> V) = x^{dim_K(V)} the order of vanishing of that determinant is dim_K(V) times ord_R(x); the cited determinant lemma turns this into the asserted equality (proof lines 361-369).
proof_roadmap: Handle the finite length case and prove the two-out-of-three principle (proof lines 329-337).
Reduce the support to {m, q} by comparing M with the sum of its localised images (proof lines 340-346).
Use the q-adic filtration to reduce to qM = 0, then to a lattice inside a one-dimensional fraction field (proof lines 347-360).
Finish with the determinant computation and the order-vanishing lemma (proof lines 361-369).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes e_R(M, 0, x) for a finite module over a Noetherian local ring with dim Supp(M) ≤ 1 and dim Supp(M/xM) ≤ 0 as the sum over the height one primes q_i of ord_{R/q_i}(x) times length_{R_{q_i}}(M_{q_i}) (statement lines 311-325). The proof is a genuine four-stage reduction: a two-out-of-three additivity argument, a comparison with the sum of the localised images, a q-adic filtration, and finally the passage to a lattice in a one-dimensional fraction field where the statement becomes a determinant computation (proof lines 329-369). The step that cannot be done by routine means is the conversion of the length of M/xM into the distance d(M, xM) and then into the order of vanishing of a determinant, which is where the numeric content of the formula sits. The claim is H2.
